title: connect.8x8.com/api/v1: JWT Algorithm Confusion Vulnerability

preconditions: Application uses JWTs for session/authorization state

process.action: Decode the JWT and inspect header/claims for algorithm and key metadata
process.expected_observation: Algorithm (HS256/RS256/none) and any embedded key/kid claim visible

process.action: Test algorithm confusion (switching RS256 to HS256 using the public key as the HMAC secret)
process.expected_observation: Server accepts the forged HS256 token signed with the public key

process.action: Test the 'none' algorithm and signature-stripping variants
process.expected_observation: Server accepts an unsigned token

process.action: Attempt to crack a weak HMAC secret offline if HS256 is used
process.expected_observation: Secret recovered, allowing arbitrary token forgery

process.action: Check for missing expiration/revocation enforcement by reusing an old or logged-out token
process.expected_observation: Expired or revoked token is still accepted

impact: Full authentication bypass via forged tokens with arbitrary claims (including admin privileges)
Persistent access via tokens that are never actually invalidated
remediation: Pin the expected algorithm server-side; never trust the algorithm specified in the token header
Use strong, sufficiently long HMAC secrets or asymmetric keys, rotated regularly
Implement short expirations plus a server-side revocation/allow-list mechanism
